target: Ju mer du övar på att prata svenska, desto mer självsäker kommer du att bli.
english: The more you practise speaking Swedish, the more confident you will become.
tip: Paired comparison uses ju ... desto: the more of one, the more of the other. Ju mer du övar, desto mer självsäker blir du.

target: Vi har ofta undrat.
english: We have often wondered.
tip: Mid-sentence adverbs like ofta go between har and the participle: Vi har ofta undrat, not har undrat ofta.

target: Tåget avgår klockan 14:35.
english: The train departs at 14:35.
tip: Swedish uses the 24-hour clock for schedules, so avgår klockan 14:35 means departs at 2:35 pm.

target: Vad han sa förvånade oss.
english: What he said surprised us.
tip: A whole clause can fill the first slot. Vad han sa works as the subject, so the verb förvånade comes right after it.

target: Henne har jag aldrig träffat.
english: Her I have never met.
tip: Front the object for emphasis and the verb stays in second place, so the subject jag follows: Henne har jag aldrig träffat.

target: Springa orkar jag inte.
english: Run I can't be bothered to.
tip: Front an infinitive for emphasis and the verb still comes second: Springa puts orkar before the subject jag.

target: Jag syns inte i mörkret.
english: I cannot be seen in the dark.
tip: The -s ending forms a passive: syns means is seen or is visible, so Jag syns inte = I cannot be seen.

target: Sällan har jag ätit så gott.
english: Seldom have I eaten so well.
tip: Starting with a restrictive adverb like sällan forces inversion, so the verb har comes before the subject jag.

target: Vi kramas vid avskedet på kvällen med vänner.
english: We exchange hugs at the farewell in the evening with friends.
tip: The -s ending can mean each other: kramas is hug one another, so Vi kramas = we hug each other.

target: Det torde vara möjligt.
english: It should presumably be possible.
tip: Torde is a formal, mostly written modal for cautious probability: det torde vara möjligt means it should presumably be possible.

target: Aldrig förr hade jag sett något sådant.
english: Never before had I seen anything like it.
tip: When Aldrig förr comes first, the verb moves ahead of the subject: hade jag (had I), not jag hade. Swedish keeps the verb in second slot.

target: Resultaten presenteras i tabell tre.
english: The results are presented in table three.
tip: "Presenteras" – s-passive is dominant in Swedish academic writing. Impersonal style.

target: Minnet av sommarens dagar värmde hennes hjärta.
english: The memory of summer days warmed her heart.
tip: Swedish genitive is just -s with no apostrophe: sommarens dagar means summer's days. Do not add an apostrophe like in English.

target: Småprat är inte lika vanligt som i andra länder.
english: Small talk is not as common as in other countries.
tip: For 'as X as', Swedish uses lika X som: inte lika vanligt som = not as common as, with the adjective between lika and som.

target: Vi har fått ett erbjudande som vi inte kan tacka nej till.
english: We have received an offer that we cannot say no to.
tip: tacka nej till = to decline, tacka ja till = to accept. The verb tacka takes the word till here, plus nej or ja.

target: I fjärran hördes ljudet av bjällror.
english: In the distance the sound of bells was heard.
tip: Adding -s to the past tense (here -des) forms the passive: hördes means was heard.

target: Hon har snart fyllt tjugo.
english: She will soon turn twenty.
tip: For reaching an age, Swedish uses "fylla" (to fill): hon har fyllt tjugo = she has turned twenty.

target: Han har ofta besökt oss.
english: He has often visited us.
tip: In a main clause a short adverb sits between "har" and the participle: har ofta besökt, not har besökt ofta.

target: Barnbidraget betalas ut varje månad.
english: Child allowance is paid out every month.
tip: The -s ending makes a passive with no helper verb: barnbidraget betalas ut = the allowance is paid out.

target: Vi hade just slagit oss ner.
english: We had just sat down.
tip: "Slå sig ner" means to sit down or settle in; the reflexive is required: vi hade slagit oss ner.

target: Jag tar en kanelbulle till kaffet.
english: I'll have a cinnamon bun with the coffee.
tip: For food and drink pairings "till" means "to go with": en kanelbulle till kaffet, a bun with the coffee.

target: Man vet aldrig vad som kan hända.
english: You never know what might happen.
tip: When "vad" is the subject of the clause that follows, add "som": vad som kan hända (what can happen), not vad kan hända.

target: Semesterlagen ger rätt till fem veckors semester.
english: The vacation law gives the right to five weeks' vacation.
tip: A length of time before a noun takes the genitive -s: fem veckors semester = five weeks of vacation.

target: Jag har precis kommit hem från en lång resa utomlands.
english: I have just come home from a long trip abroad.
tip: Swedish builds the perfect with "har" even for motion verbs: jag har kommit hem, never "är kommit".

target: Den trettonde december firar vi Lucia med familjen.
english: On the thirteenth of December we celebrate Lucia with the family.
tip: When a time phrase opens the sentence, the verb stays second, before the subject: den trettonde december firar vi.

target: Det lär dröja innan vi ser resultat.
english: It's likely to be a while before we see results.
tip: "Lär" + infinitive = is likely to / will probably.

target: Tåget blev försenat.
english: The train got delayed.
tip: blev plus a participle like försenat marks a change that happened to the subject, unlike vara which just states a fact.

target: Vi hjälptes åt att bära.
english: We helped each other carry.
tip: hjälptes åt uses the -s to mean each other, so hjälptes åt att bära = helped one another carry, not a passive.

target: Med facit i hand hade vi rätt.
english: In hindsight we were right.
tip: "Med facit i hand" = with the answer key in hand – in hindsight.

target: Boken skrevs av Astrid Lindgren.
english: The book was written by Astrid Lindgren.
tip: Add -s to make the passive: skrevs = was written. The doer follows av, so skrevs av Astrid Lindgren means written by her.
